source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
For the first identified emission event, look at the data. Do you see a spike? If so, choose the date that represents the start of the spike (or if it doesn't spike up it may plateau at an elevated level - use that date as the event start).
3. Do the same thing for the end of the event.
4. Plot this time frame in a chart and show the elevation above the background level.
5. Calculate the ppm above background. Calculate the ppm-hours.
6. Convert ppm-hours to ppb-hours.
7. Calculate how much ppm has to be at the sample site to increase the background concentration by 1 ppb on the day of the event. Use the background concentration from the nearest air monitoring station as a proxy for the level of the air at the sample site.
8. Multiply this by the ppm-hours above background to arrive at the ppb-hours for this event
